skill.name: brainstorming
skill.description: Guides collaborative brainstorming before creative or implementation work by clarifying intent, requirements, constraints, and design trade-offs.
skill.summary: Turns early ideas into validated designs through structured questions, options, and documentation.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by an inline Markdown filename pattern on SKILL.md:38. I found no executable code, prompt injection attempt, data exfiltration intent, or other semantic security issue in the reviewed skill text.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md:38 contains an inline Markdown path template for a design document, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The file is prompt-only and does not execute this text as a command.

content.value_statement: Early ideas often move into implementation before goals, constraints, and success criteria are clear. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code guide structured discovery, compare approaches, and produce a validated design plan.
actual_capabilities: Reviews current project files, documentation, and recent commits before design discussion.
Asks one focused question at a time to clarify purpose, constraints, and success criteria.
Proposes two or three implementation approaches with trade-offs and a recommendation.
Presents the design in short sections that cover architecture, components, data flow, errors, and tests.
Writes the validated design to a planned documentation path when documentation is requested.
limitations: It depends on user answers and available project context to form a complete design.
It does not implement the feature by itself during the brainstorming phase.
It may reference companion skills that are useful only when they are installed.
It cannot guarantee business correctness without domain review from the user.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Product Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a rough product idea into requirements, constraints, user flows, and success criteria before engineering starts.

use_cases.title: Compare Technical Approaches
use_cases.description: Evaluate multiple architecture or implementation options with trade-offs before choosing a direction.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Design Document
use_cases.description: Create a validated design outline that covers architecture, components, data flow, error handling, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Start Feature Discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to help me shape this idea into a clear feature plan. Ask one question at a time and start with the most important missing context: [idea].

prompt_templates.title: Refine Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to clarify requirements for [feature]. Focus on user goals, constraints, success criteria, and what we should exclude.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementation Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to propose two or three approaches for [feature]. Include trade-offs, risks, and your recommended option.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Validated Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to produce a design for [feature]. Cover architecture, components, data flow, error handling, tests, and documentation after validating each section with me.

output_examples.input: I want to add team invitations to our app.
output: First clarification question about who can invite users and what roles are allowed.
A comparison of invitation link, email invite, and admin-created account approaches.
A validated design section covering permissions, token expiry, user states, and tests.

output_examples.input: We need a better dashboard for customer support agents.
output: A short discovery flow that clarifies agent tasks, key metrics, and speed constraints.
Recommended dashboard layout options with trade-offs for density and navigation.
A design outline for data loading, empty states, errors, and acceptance tests.

output_examples.input: Help me plan a refactor of our billing settings.
output: Focused questions about current pain points, migration limits, and affected users.
Two or three refactor approaches with risk and testing implications.
A documentation-ready design plan for modules, data flow, rollout, and validation.

best_practices: Start with a concise idea and let the skill ask focused follow-up questions.
Share relevant project constraints, existing documentation, and success criteria early.
Review each design section before moving to implementation planning.
anti_patterns: Skipping discovery questions and asking for a full design from incomplete context.
Using the skill as a substitute for stakeholder or domain review.
Moving into implementation before trade-offs and acceptance criteria are agreed.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps turn early ideas into clear designs through questions, approach comparisons, and incremental validation.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on brainstorming, requirements, and design before implementation begins.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow asks the assistant to inspect project files, documentation, and recent commits before planning.

faq.question: How many options will it compare?
faq.answer: It normally proposes two or three approaches and explains trade-offs before recommending one.

faq.question: Does it create documentation?
faq.answer: It can write the validated design to a planned document path when the environment and permissions allow it.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
